50-115.r: Brahmo Samaj → Kolkata (1828); Manav Dharma Sabha → Surat; Arya Samaj → Mumbai (1875); Nadwah-ul-Ulama → Lucknow.

50-116.r: Jury Act of 1826 → only Christians could be jurors in trials of Christians, Hindus/Muslims could not; strongly opposed by Raja Ram Mohan Roy.

50-117.r: Prarthana Samaj → Mahadev Govind Ranade; Ramakrishna Mission → Swami Vivekananda; Satyashodhak Samaj → Jyotiba Phule; Muhammadan Anglo-Oriental College, Aligarh → Sir Syed Ahmed Khan.

50-118.r: Both correct: Justice Party (Madras Presidency, 1916, non-Brahmin) called Congress Brahmin-dominated and sought communal representation for non-Brahmins like Muslims got under Morley-Minto reforms.

50-119.r: Brahmo Samaj → Raja Ram Mohan Roy; Ramakrishna Mission → Swami Vivekananda; Servants of India Society → Gopal Krishna Gokhale; Vidhva Vivah Samaj → Vishnu Shastri Pandit.

50-120.r: Poona Sarvajanik Sabha → launched 2 April 1870 at Pune by G.V. Joshi, S.H. Sathe, S.H. Chiplonkar and others; M.G. Ranade joined in November 1871.
50-120.t: Not founded by Ranade; he joined later, so 'None of the above' is right.

50-121.r: Servants of India Society → Gopal Krishna Gokhale, 1905 (correct pair). Tatvabodhini Sabha → Devendra Nath Tagore (1839), not Keshav Chandra Sen.
hi: Servants of India Society (भारत सेवक समाज)

50-122.r: Servants of India Society (Gokhale, 1905) → distinguished members M.C. Setalvad, B.N. Rao, Alladi Krishnaswami Iyer; also V. Srinivas Shastri, N.M. Joshi, H.N. Kunzru.
hi: Servants of India Society (भारत सेवक समाज)

50-127.r: Servants of India Society → founded by G.K. Gokhale in 1905; first secular body serving unprivileged rural and tribal people.

50-128.r: Servants of India Society → Gopal Krishna Gokhale; Tattvabodhini Sabha → Debendranath Tagore; Atmiya Sabha → Raja Ram Mohan Roy.

50-130.r: Servants of India Society → founded 12 June 1905 by Gokhale at Fergusson Hill, Pune, with Natesh Appaji Dravid, G.K. Deodhar and Anant Vinayak Patwardhan.

50-131.r: K.M. Panikkar → called Gopal Krishna Gokhale 'the first diplomat of modern India'.

50-132.r: Bahujan Samaj → founded by Mukund Rao Patil and Shankar Rao Jadhav against exploitation of lower castes by Brahmins, moneylenders and landlords; opposed Congress.
50-132.t: Not B.R. Ambedkar: Bahujan Samaj here is Mukund Rao Patil's body.

50-133.r: Nadars → demanded the right to enter temples, causing a terrible riot in Tirunelveli (Tamil Nadu) in 1899.

50-134.r: "If God were to tolerate untouchability, I would not recognize him as God at all" → Bal Gangadhar Tilak.
50-134.t: Sounds like Gandhi or Ambedkar, but the quote is Tilak's.

50-135.r: Ram Mohan Roy → purest Hinduism is in the Upanishads; Keshav Chandra Sen → Brahmovad as world religion; Dayanand → Hinduism = Vedic religion; Ramakrishna → many ways to God.

50-136.r: Wrong pair: Raja Ram Mohan Roy–Adi Brahma Samaj. Roy founded Brahmo Samaj (20 August 1828); 'Adi Brahmo Samaj' was Debendra Nath Tagore's group after the 1866 split.
50-136.t: Adi Brahmo Samaj = Devendra Nath Tagore; Bhartiya Brahmo Samaj = Keshav Chandra Sen.

50-137.r: Wrong pair: Bahishkrit Hitkarini Sabha → B.R. Ambedkar, not Jyotiba Phule. Correct: Young Bengal–Derozio; Theosophical Society–Colonel Olcott; United Indian Patriotic Association–Syed Ahmad Khan.

50-138.r: D.K. Karve → Secretary, Widow Remarriage Association; J.E.D. Bethune → girls' school in Calcutta; Vidyasagar → Principal, Sanskrit College Calcutta; B.M. Malabari → crusade against child marriage.

50-139.r: Prarthana Samaj → Atmaram Pandurang; Young India → Gandhi; Lokahitavadi → Gopal Hari Deshmukh; Satyashodhak Samaj → Jyotiba Phule; Rehnumai Mazdayasan Sabha → Naoroji Furdonji.

50-140.r: Sanatan Dharma Rakshini Sabha → Calcutta (correct). Others: Bharat Dharma Mahamandal → Haridwar; Deva Samaj → Lahore; Radhaswami Satsang → Agra.

50-141.r: Dayanand Saraswati, Ishwar Chandra Vidyasagar and Raja Ram Mohan Roy → all three were proficient in Sanskrit.

50-142.r: All true: Brahmo Samaj → monotheism; Arya Samaj → helped develop education; Swami Vivekananda → founded Ramakrishna Mission (1897).

50-143.r: Women's movement in India → largely inspired by Jyotiba Phule (opened India's first girls' school, 1848); Ramabai Ranade (Seva Sadan) also inspired it.
50-143.c: Printed answer Jyotiba Phule, but explanation says BPSC starred the question: Ramabai Ranade was intended (option misprinted 'Padmabai Ranaday').

50-144.r: Brahmo Samaj, Ramakrishna Mission and Arya Samaj → none had a political mission, but all helped develop a spirit of patriotism.

50-145.r: False: Gandhi born in Gandhinagar (he was born 2 October 1869 at Porbandar). True: Annie Besant a Theosophist; Theosophical headquarters in Madras; Dayanand founded Arya Samaj.

50-146.r: All correct: Anti-Untouchability League (1932, later Harijan Sevak Sangh) → Gandhi; All India Kisan Sabha (1936, Lucknow) → Sahajanand Saraswati; Self-Respect Movement → Periyar E.V. Ramaswami Naicker.

50-148.r: Neo-Buddhism (Dalit Buddhist movement, new sect 'Navayan') → Dr. B.R. Ambedkar.

50-149.r: Dar-ul-Ulum of Nadwatul Ulama, Lucknow (1898) → linked to Maulana Shibli Numani, who with Maulana Lutfullah founded Nadwatul Ulama at Kanpur, 1893.

50-150.r: Paramahansa Mandali → secret socio-religious group of Bombay (Maharashtra), founded by Dadoba Pandurang Tarkhadkar; promoted monotheism; began religious reform in Bombay.

50-152.r: Deoband Movement → began 1866 at Deoband (Saharanpur, U.P.); founders incl. Muhammad Qasim Nanotavi, Rashid Ahmed Gangohi; aim to overthrow British rule.

50-153.r: Faraizi Movement → begun by Haji Shariatullah; against British rule that curbed Muslims' religious freedom and rights.

50-155.r: Tarkeswar Movement (Bengal, 1924) → against corruption in temples: the Mahants of Tarkeswar Shiva temple harassed pilgrims and made unjust money demands.

50-157.r: Abhinav Bharat Society → V.D. Savarkar renamed 'Mitra Mela' (started with brother Ganesh Damodar Savarkar) as Abhinav Bharat at Nashik in 1904.

51-001.r: Zamindari Association (Landholders' Society), Calcutta, 1838 → first political organisation in India; Dwarkanath Tagore and landlords; protected landlords' interests by constitutional means.

51-002.r: Both true, R explains A: Bengal British Indian Society (1843) → result of George Thompson's efforts (its president), whom Dwarkanath Tagore brought from England.

51-003.r: Poona Sarvajanik Sabha (Pune, 2 April 1870) → in 1875 petitioned the House of Commons for India's direct representation in British Parliament.

51-004.r: Indian Association → founded 26 July 1876, Calcutta, by Surendranath Banerjee with Anand Mohan Bose; most important pre-Congress nationalist body; favoured middle class over landlords.

51-008.r: Surendra Nath Banerjee → dismissed from the Civil Services in 1874 for a minor judicial error.

51-009.r: Surendranath Banerji → selected for ICS (1869), disqualified over age, reinstated by court, then dismissed for a minor judicial error; later founded Indian Association and Indian National Conference.

51-010.r: Indian National Conference (Surendranath Banerjee) → merged with the Indian National Congress in 1886, as both had the same aims.

51-011.r: Raja Ram Mohan Roy → first Indian to agitate for political reforms (per Bipin Chandra Pal); some historians credit Surendra Nath Banerjee.

51-012.r: Order: Bombay Association (August 1852, Dadabhai Naoroji) → Indian League (September 1875, Shishir Kumar Ghosh) → Indian Association (July 1876) → Madras Mahajan Sabha (May 1884).
51-012.h: B-I-I-M: Bombay, India League, Indian Association, Madras.

51-014.r: Pherozeshah Mehta → a founder and president of the Bombay Presidency Association (1885); urged Indians to take up Western education.

51-015.r: Bombay Presidency Association (1885) → founded by Pherozeshah Mehta, K.T. Tailang and Badruddin Tyabji together, so 'More than one of the above'.

51-016.r: Mismatched: East India Association (1866, Dadabhai Naoroji) → London, not Calcutta; Indian Association (1876, S.N. Banerjee) → Kolkata, not Bombay. British India Society (1839, William Adam) → London.
51-016.t: National Indian Association (1870/71, Mary Carpenter) was also in London.

51-017.r: Book's key: Indian Association → Surendranath Banerjee; Madras Mahajan Sabha → M. Veeraraghavachariar; Bombay Presidency Association → Dadabhai Naoroji; Poona Sarvajanik Sabha → Justice Ranade.
51-017.c: Pairing Bombay Presidency Association with Dadabhai Naoroji clashes with other entries crediting Pherozeshah Mehta, Telang, Tyabji.

51-018.r: Book's key: 'The Indian Association' (Bristol Indian Association of 1870, renamed National Indian Association in 1871; Mary Carpenter, Keshav Chandra Sen) worked for women's education, so was not political.
51-018.c: Doubtful: explanation uses the Bristol body; S.N. Banerjee's Indian Association was itself a pre-Congress political association.

51-019.r: Both true, R explains A: Dadabhai Naoroji → East India Association, London, 1866, to influence British public opinion on Indian questions.

51-020.r: Order: Bangabhasha Prakasika Sabha (1836) → Landholders' Society (1838, Dwarkanath Tagore) → Bengal British India Society (1843) → Indian League (1875, Shishir Kumar Ghose).

51-021.r: Land Holders' Society → Dwarkanath Tagore; British India Society → William Adams; Indian Society → Anand Mohan Bose; Indian Association → S.N. Banerji.

51-022.r: Order: East India Association (1866, Naoroji) → National Indian Association (1870/71, Mary Carpenter) → Indian Society (1872, Anand Mohan Bose) → Indian Association (1876).

51-023.r: India League → Shishir Kumar Ghosh (1875); Indian Association → Anand Mohan Bose (1876); Indian National Liberal Federation → Surendranath Banerjee; United Indian Patriotic Association → Syed Ahmad Khan.

51-024.r: Indian Association → Surendra Nath Banerjee; Poona Sarvajanik Sabha → Mahadev Govind Ranade; Bombay Presidency Association → Pherozeshah Mehta; Madras Mahajan Sabha → Anand Charlu.

51-025.r: United Indian Patriotic Association (1888) → founded by Sir Syed Ahmed Khan and Raja Shiv Prasad of Banaras.

51-026.r: Asiatic Society of Bengal → 1784; of Bombay → 1804. Wrong: Royal Asiatic Society of Great Britain was 1823 (not 1813); Land Holders Society 1838 (not 1844).
51-026.c: No answer printed: two options, (c) and (d), are both wrong.

51-027.r: Asiatic Society of Bengal, Calcutta → founded 1784 by William Jones.
51-027.t: Not Warren Hastings or Jonathan Duncan; founder is William Jones.

51-028.r: Asiatic Society of Bengal → founded 15 January 1784 by Sir William Jones, a British lawyer and Orientalist, to encourage Oriental studies.
